45aa69400a.q: How does the IRS use statistical algorithms to select tax cases for audit?
45aa69400a.a: The IRS uses a scientific algorithm method where they collect statistical data from other types of audits. They then compare someone in industry A to other data for people in industry A, and if something appears off, it could trigger an audit. The IRS is very transparent about this process and posts this information on their website.

3ff46e1539.q: How much can whistleblowers earn through the IRS whistleblower program?
3ff46e1539.a: Whistleblowers can get paid between 10 to 25 percent through the IRS whistleblower program. There is an online process for the average everyday person who is aware of something shady going on to report that to the IRS.

54101416a2.q: What is the earned income tax credit fraud scheme that preparers create with false Schedule C forms?
54101416a2.a: Some preparers create complete fake Schedule C forms on returns to get the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). In many cases, they create fictitious income or business losses for clients, sometimes without the clients' knowledge. The clients receive refunds they are not entitled to, and a portion goes to the Social Security Administration as self-employment tax, allowing them to later qualify for Social Security benefits despite never actually working those jobs.

5666b76c34.q: What are the three main IRS divisions that handle most audit and investigation work?
5666b76c34.a: The three main divisions are TEG (Tax Exempt Government Entities), SBSE (Small Business Self-Employed) for taxpayers with $10 million in assets or less, and Large Case (also called LBI) for larger business taxpayers. Most audit work and investigations happen within one of these three major divisions.

1ff4ae92eb.q: How do IRS revenue agents investigate embezzlement discovered during routine tax audits?
1ff4ae92eb.a: When a revenue agent discovers signs of embezzlement during an audit, they follow the same investigative process: reviewing the return, requesting bank statements and financial records through an IDR (Information Document Request), analyzing the source of funds and where money went, looking for unexplained deposits and irregularities, and presenting findings in a report. The work is similar to what forensic accountants do—following the money to determine what actually happened.
